title: I Let the Hybrid-Office Desk-Hoteling Policy Survive Three Relocations

parts.text: I booked desk K12 on Monday under the hoteling policy HR launched with balloons. I arrived to a director's family photos taped to the monitor. I was thirty-one, twice-a-week hybrid, holding a laptop stand. The policy said no personalization overnight. I photographed the photos, the booking, the balloon email. Then I stacked the frames in a labeled box at lost and found. At 9:20 the director asked who boxed her kids.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: She wants the kids back on a desk the balloon email said nobody owns.

social.video_title: Balloons launched hoteling; her photos overnighted on K12 — Part 1/3
social.description: Monday booking, family frames, lost-and-found box. Would you have left the photos up?

parts.text: HR said the policy applied. She moved to K14 on Tuesday and taped the photos again. I had booked K14 because the app allowed it. I boxed them again, same label. She cc'd my manager about hostility. My manager had the balloon PDF. Wednesday she tried a third desk in another neighborhood of the floor. The app still let me book it if I woke up at 6. I woke up at 6.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: Wednesday's third neighborhood is on my 6 a.m. confirmation.

social.video_title: K14 got the same box; she fled to another neighborhood — Part 2/3
social.description: Hostility cc, balloon PDF, 6 a.m. booking. Would you have let her keep one island?

parts.text: Facilities issued lockable pedestals for directors who need photos, which is a real solution. Hoteling survived. I sit where I book. She sits with a pedestal. Balloons came down. The PDF did not. Three relocations taught the floor that overnight tape is not a lease. I still come twice a week. The laptop stand fits every K. Kids belong in pedestals or at home, not on my booked glass. Policy lived. That was the point of the balloons.

social.description: Hoteling held, photos housed, PDF forever. Was a balloon a nameplate?
